This is game 16 in a series of 9×9 Go games. Each new game starts in a fresh session.

## Your goal

To become as strong at Go as you can: to keep improving, game after game, toward grandmaster-level play. The concrete target is to win consistently against the strongest opponent on the ladder, the 9d profile.

## What carries over

This session starts with no memory of the earlier ones: your conversation is not carried over. Your working directory does carry over: every file in it stays as you leave it. If CLAUDE.md exists there, it is loaded into your context at the start of every session; your other files are there to read with the file tools. What a later session knows of your earlier games is what you have left in these files.

Your working directory holds:
- CLAUDE.md (13,808 bytes)
- games.md (24,939 bytes)
- libs.py (813 bytes)

## This game

A new game. You play White, so your opponent moves first, right after you choose it.

Rules: Chinese area scoring, with 7 points of komi for White; a level score is a draw. Simple ko: an immediate recapture is refused, and the board marks the ko point when there is one. Suicide is not allowed. An invalid move is refused with the rule it broke, and the turn stays with you. The game ends after two passes in a row or a resignation; a game that reaches 243 moves is scored where it stands. After two passes the engine scores the position as it stands and decides itself which stones are dead.

## Opponents

Your opponent is KataGo playing in the style of a human of the rank you choose. The ladder, weakest to strongest: 20k, 18k, 16k, 14k, 12k, 10k, 8k, 6k, 4k, 2k, 1d, 3d, 5d, 7d, 9d. You choose the rank with `choose_opponent(rank)` before the first move; it holds for the whole game, and you choose again in the next game.

## Tools

- Go: `choose_opponent(rank)`, `board()`, `play(move)` with a point or `pass`, and `resign()`.
- Files: your Read, Write, Edit, Glob and Grep tools, for any file in your working directory.

You also have a shell, and you may write and run code in it; Python is available as `python3`. Use it only to inspect the current position and keep records — for example, to count stones or liberties, or check whether a move is legal. Do not build or use a Go engine, run Monte Carlo, search over sequences of future moves, or write a program that chooses, ranks or recommends moves.

## How this session ends

Play until the game is over. The final result comes back from your last Go call, followed by a closing note. Before you end the session after a game, write down in your working directory whatever will help the next session play better. The session ends when you end your turn.
I should quickly check games.md, especially the recent entries, and look over libs.py.

# Usage: python3 libs.py <<< "board rows 9..1 as 9 lines of X/O/." ; prints groups and liberties
import sys
cols="ABCDEFGHJ"
rows=[l.split() for l in sys.stdin.read().strip().splitlines()]
rows=[r[1:10] if len(r)>9 else r for r in rows]
B={}
for i,r in enumerate(rows):
    for j,c in enumerate(r): B[(j,9-i)]=c
def nb(p):
    x,y=p
    for q in((x+1,y),(x-1,y),(x,y+1),(x,y-1)):
        if q in B: yield q
seen=set()
for p in B:
    if B[p] in"XO" and p not in seen:
        g=[p];libs=set();k=0;seen.add(p)
        while k<len(g):
            for q in nb(g[k]):
                if B[q]=='.':libs.add(q)
                elif B[q]==B[p] and q not in seen: seen.add(q);g.append(q)
            k+=1
        n=lambda s:",".join(sorted(cols[a]+str(b) for a,b in s))
        print(B[p],n(g),"libs:",len(libs),n(libs))
n atari
  -> lost H4 plus H5/J4/J5 (~5 pts). A hane stone at 2 libs must be connected (H5) before
  invading elsewhere (lesson 1 again!).
- Bottom invasion (G3/F3/E2/F2/G2/E1) died: 3 libs, eye space E1-G1 only, W H1/D1 took both
  ends. The white chain had only 2 libs (D3,H4) but both were unreachable (D3 suicide while
  D2/C3 white, H4 surrounded). Don't count liberties I can't legally fill.

## Game 12 — White vs 16k — DRAW (White 37 area + 7 = Black 44)
Moves: B E5, W C4, B C5 (attach on top), W G6, B G5 (attach under), W D7, B D4, W C3, B D3,
W D2, B E2, W C2, B B5, W E6!, B F5, W F6 (solid, fills F6 cut), B H6, W H7, B J6, W G7
(fills G7 cut), B B4, W B3, B A3, W A2 (atari), B A4, W B1 (eyes A1+B2), B D1, W C1,
B E1, W C6, B B6, W C7, B B8 (invasion), W B7 (cut), B C8, W D8, B A7, W C9, B D5, W B9
(atari), B A8, W J7, B H4, W D6, B A6 (B8 group connected out via A7-A6-B6), W G3 (free
invasion, died: B H3, W G2, B F3, W H2, B J2, W D9, B A9, W F2, B G4), pass pass.
Takeaways:
- Opening vs tengen worked much better than G6/G10: two separated stones (C4 low-left, G6
  upper-right) and then D7 + E6 made a TOP framework (rows 6-9) while the C4 corner lived small.
  Black's row-5 wall (B5-G5) scored only rows 1-5. Final split: my top ~27 + corner 10 = 37.
- E6 (head of E5, linking D7/G6) was the key sealing move; then F6/G7 solid fills meant no cuts.
- The bottom-left corner cost 6 moves (C3, D2, C2, B3, A2, B1, C1) for 10 points; B1 gave
  guaranteed eyes A1+B2 (stones A2/B1/B3/C2 around them). Eye shape note: after B A3/A4 hane,
  W A2 + B1 = two real eyes even if black takes D1.
- LOST THE WIN on the top-left: B B8 invasion connected back to its B6 wall via A7-A6, taking
  A6-A9,B8,C8 (~6 pts of my top). My B7 stone could not stop A7/A6. The fix was earlier: when B
  pushed B6 against my C6, block on B7 (or play the 2-2-ish B8 myself) BEFORE black pokes in;
  my C7 left the B7/B8/A7 corner open. A 1-2 point margin game was decided by that corner.
- W B9 atari forced A8 but left B9-C9 at 2 libs (A9,D9) => black A9 was sente for them. A9
  decided win/draw: 37 vs 38 points. Consider playing D9 first (calm) so A9 is gote for both.
- Late invasion G3 into black's bottom (E-J cols, rows 1-4, black H4 already there) died as
  expected; it was free under area scoring (black answered inside own area) but gained nothing.

## Game 13 — Black vs 14k — LOSS W+2 (Black 43 area vs 38+7)
Moves: B C4, W F6, B F4, W C6, B E5, W E6, B G6? (hane at head), W G5! (crosscut), B F5,
W G7 (G6 atari), B G4, W H5, B H4, W H6 (captures G6), B B6, W B7, B B5 (B6 had 2 libs), W A6,
B A5, W A7, B C5, W D6, B C8 (invasion), W C7, B E8, W F8, B D7, W E7 (D7 in atari), B D8,
W B8, B J5, W J6, B J4, W D5! (poke, forces D4), B D4, W E9, B G9, W F9, B H8, W G8, B H9,
W H7, B B9, W D9, pass pass. Final: Black rows 1-4 + A5,B5,C5,E5,F5,J5 + B6 = 43.
Takeaways:
- After C4/F4/E5 vs W C6/F6/E6 the board was an even row-5 split: rows 1-5 = 45 = WIN. I only
  had to hold row 5 SOLIDLY. Instead B G6 hane (stone touching F6 with W free to crosscut G5)
  lost G5/H5 and the G6 stone (~3 pts) => that alone was the margin. When the split already
  wins, play solid boundary moves (G5/F5, D5), not hanes into the opponent's side.
- D5 was a 1-pt boundary point I never took; W D5 later was sente (forced D4). Before
  invading/probing, take the boundary points that are sente for the opponent.
- Top invasion C8/E8/D7/D8 (move 24) never had eye space: W walls on row 6-7 + B8/F8/E9 hanes
  left a straight-three on row 9. Invading a 3-row-deep area behind a complete wall = dead
  (lesson W1 again). It cost nothing in area scoring but gained nothing either.
- B6/B5/A5 left-side push gained ~2 points (good): B6 was undercutting C6 with C4 support.

## Game 14 — White vs 16k — LOSS B+2 (White 36 area + 7 = 43 vs 45)
Moves: B E5, W C4, B E3 (approach under C4), W G6, B G4, W D6, B E6 (push between D6/G6),
W E7 (hane at head), B D5 (cuts D6 from C4), W D7 (D6 had 2 libs), B C5, W C6, B C3 (C4 now
2 libs, effectively dead), W F6, B G5, W B5, B B4 (C4 atari), W B6 (B5 had 2 libs: B6 cut
was an atari), B H6!, W H7, B J6, W J7, B H4, W F5 (1 pt, B F4), W G7 (F5-G6 group had 2 libs),
B A4, W G2 (invasion), B F2, W G3, B F3, W H3, B H1! (placement), W J2, B G1, W H2, B F1,
W J4, B H5 (J5 now kills: J4 atari -> J3 eye false), W A5, B D4 (captures C4), W E2, B D2,
pass pass.
Final split: White rows 7-9 (27) + A6-D6,F6,G6 + A5,B5,F5 = 36. Black everything else.
Takeaways:
- LOST C4 (~whole lower-left) with my 3rd move D6: vs B E5+E3, D6 is on the far side of
  E5 from C4; B pushed E6 then cut D5/C5 and C3 boxed C4 in. Then C4 was a dead stone and
  B5/B6 were gote fixes. Vs a black approach (E3) under my C4, my next move must either
  give C4 a base (D3/C3-ish or C6 for an extension up the side) or I accept losing it and
  must then get the WHOLE right side top-to-row-5 instead. Don't leave a lone stone 2 lines
  from 3 black stones.
- Move 20 B H6 (then J6) took H6/J6/H5/J5: exactly my 2-point margin. Each side's row-6 point
  (H6) was as big as anything; I was forced to play B6 first because B5 had 2 libs. B5 was a
  gote stone that needed a second move — play B6 (solid) directly instead of B5 next time.
- F5 poke between E5/G5 (with F6 support) gained a point and was safe.
- Invasion G2 into a 4-wide bottom strip (F-J, rows 1-3) under a row-4 wall: black F2, F3,
  H1 (placement on 1st line under 2-2) killed it. J4 extension made J3 an eye only if J4
  survived, but J5 (next to black J6) ataried J4 -> false eye. Corner invasions need the
  far side (J4/J5) not to touch black stones.

## Game 15 — Black vs 14k — WIN B+10 (Black 49 area vs 32+7)
Moves: B C4, W E5 (tengen), B G6 (other side, high), W C6, B F4, W E4 (wedge), B E3 (hane
under), W F5, B G5 (hane at head of two), W D3 (cut), B F3 (solid; avoids double atari at F3),
W D4, B C3, W D2, B C2, W F7, B G7, W F8, B E2, W H8 (probe), B G8! (cut it from F8), W G9,
B H7, W H9, B J8, W F6, B C5, W D5, B B6 (safe: read W B5 cut fails), W C7, B B7, W B8, B J7,
W F9, B D1, W H3 (invasion), B H4 (pushes it into the small corner + covers G4 cut via
self-atari), W G3, B G4 (must: W G4 would cut three groups), W J3, B G2 (vital pt of base),
W A8, B H2 (W left with 2 libs, dead), W A7, B B5 (B6-B7 had 2 libs; A6 would have lost them),
W A6, B A5, W C8, B J9, W pass, B J4, W D6, B J2 (captured 3), W E7, pass pass.
Takeaways:
- vs W tengen: C4 + G6 (diagonal opposite sides) then F4 made an L-shaped area: bottom rows
  1-4 + right side cols G-J. W's wedge E4/D3/D4/D2 cut through the middle but my two sides
  were each solid -> W got only the top-left + center (32).
- Counting each move (needed 45; had ~48-50 from move 30) made the endgame easy: solid
  moves (B5 not A6, J7 not J9) kept everything.
- Killing the late H3 invasion: H4 from the open side (toward my bigger area), G4 to keep my
  groups connected, then G2/H2 vital points on the 2nd line -> white had 2 libs, no eyes.

I'm examining the liberties around F4 after a black hane at G4, since that stone now has only two liberties and is in danger. I'm checking whether white should hane at G3 or reinforce directly, tracing through how black might respond by cutting or atari-ing to see if the group holds together.

Thinking more broadly about the whole board, I'm estimating territory — white likely needs most of the left side plus the bottom to reach around 38-39 points, which is close, so I need to defend F4 efficiently. I'm comparing a solid connection at F3 versus a more aggressive G3 hane, weighing how black's likely E4 cut plays out and whether white can turn it into an atari.

Considering W G3 instead as a more aggressive alternative, taking more of the bottom but inviting black's hane at G3/H3 push. Checking the cut at E4 again under this line: it ataris F4, so I extend to F3, forming a group with F4/G3 that has decent liberties, while black's E4 and G4 stones remain weak and need follow-up, keeping me ahead in this exchange.

Still, cutting at E4 looks messy for my bottom stones, so I'm leaning toward just playing F3 solidly instead and rereading the ladder after W D5 atari to confirm black's cutting group can't escape.

Continuing the ladder, each chase reduces black's liberties further—C2, B2, C1, D1—and it looks like black can't escape since my surrounding stones are solid. This is a deep cut into my territory but the ladder should favor me and let black's group die.

Rather than chasing this atari sequence further, maybe D4 atari is cleaner, but I'll hold that for later. I'll just play F3.

I won game 16 as White against the 16k opponent, by 4 points (W+4): 39 area points plus 7 komi makes 46, against Black's 42. It's my first win as White in this series, so my record as White is now 1-7-1 (wins-losses-draws); as Black it's still 3-4.

**How it went:**
- **Opening:** Black opened with G6 and D7 to build a framework across the top. I played C4, then took E5, the center point between those two black stones.
- **Middle game:** When Black attached at F5, I played hane underneath at F4. Each time one of my stones dropped to two liberties I connected it right away (F3, E4). When Black wedged in at D4, I answered underneath at D3, and the C5 atari that followed forced Black's reply.
- **Endgame:** I closed the edges in this order: G3, C6, B7, H3, J2, H2, A6, then C3. My area ended up as the bottom three rows plus the left side up to row 6.
- **Late invasion:** After Black passed, I tried a free invasion at H7 inside Black's top-right area. It died, as earlier invasions behind a finished wall have. It didn't change the score.

- **`games.md`:** the full move list for game 16 and what I learned from it.
- **`CLAUDE.md`:** the updated ladder status and a new section on the opening that won. It notes that 39 is a thin margin and solid connecting moves have to continue. The next suggested games are Black vs 12k, then White vs 14k.
